answers.stem_only: gp3: random small I/O at 10,000 IOPS needs SSD; gp3 includes a baseline of IOPS independent of size and lets you buy extra IOPS cheaply, so provision 10,000 IOPS on a 2 TiB gp3 volume. io2 costs more and HDD types cannot do random IOPS.

Daily EBS snapshots (stored regionally, not tied to one AZ); after an AZ failure, create a volume from the latest snapshot in another AZ of the same Region and attach it to a new instance. RPO 1 day and RTO hours fit; no cross-Region copy or standby needed.
Instance store: temporary, re-creatable scratch data with lowest latency, physically attached NVMe disks included in the instance price.
Root volumes default to DeleteOnTermination = true; set DeleteOnTermination to false for the root volume in the block device mapping of the launch template.
Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager with daily snapshots and 7-day retention, and delete older snapshots; deleting older incremental snapshots does not break newer ones because needed blocks are kept.

EBS volumes cannot be shrunk with Elastic Volumes, and a volume restored from a snapshot cannot be smaller than the snapshot's source size. Create a new smaller gp3 volume (sized for data plus growth, e.g. a few hundred GiB), copy data at file level, switch over in a maintenance window, delete the old volume.
Amazon EFS (Regional, multi-AZ) mounted by every instance via NFS: shared file semantics across AZs with no replication jobs to manage.
Enable EBS fast snapshot restore on the snapshot in the fleet's AZ so new volumes are fully initialized at creation, with no pre-warming scripts.
Data Lifecycle Manager (or AWS Backup) policy for daily snapshots with 30-day retention, plus a Recycle Bin retention rule for EBS snapshots that keeps deleted snapshots for at least 7 days.
One io2 Block Express volume with 12,000 provisioned IOPS: io2 gives the highest EBS durability (99.999%) and sub-millisecond latency; gp3 has lower durability, and mirroring doubles the cost.

Snapshots encrypted with the AWS managed key cannot be shared and its key policy cannot be edited. Copy each snapshot re-encrypted with a customer managed key, grant only the backup account use of that key, share the copies with only the backup account (which then ideally copies them under its own key).
Use Elastic Volumes to increase the gp3 volume size online, then extend the partition and file system inside the OS; no stop needed.

EBS Multi-Attach on an io1/io2 (Provisioned IOPS) volume attached to both Nitro instances in the same AZ, formatted with a cluster-aware file system so writes are coordinated; standard file systems like XFS/ext4 are not safe for simultaneous mounts, and gp3 does not support Multi-Attach.
The bottleneck is the instance's EBS IOPS limit (15,000), not the volumes (24,000 provisioned). Move to a larger Nitro instance type with a higher EBS IOPS limit.
Throughput Optimized HDD (st1): frequently accessed, large sequential reads such as log processing; cheaper per GB than SSD and faster than sc1, which is for infrequent access.
gp2 at 100 GiB gives only about 300 baseline IOPS. Modify the volume online to gp3 with Elastic Volumes and provision 8,000 IOPS at the same 100 GiB size; cheaper than growing gp2 or moving to io2.
Data must survive stop/start, so not instance store. Per-instance gp3 EBS volume: SSD random I/O, persistent, cheaper than EFS and no sharing needed.

EBS Snapshot Lock in compliance mode for one year: nobody, including the root user and administrators, can delete the snapshot or shorten the lock once the cooling-off period (optional) has passed; governance mode and IAM denies can be undone by privileged admins.

Enable EBS encryption by default in the Region for all new volumes; for the existing unencrypted volume, snapshot it, copy the snapshot with encryption (or create an encrypted volume from the snapshot), and swap volumes. Existing volumes cannot be encrypted in place.
EBS encryption by default is a per-Region account setting: turn it on in both Regions; the AWS managed key (aws/ebs) is enough since no key control is required.
Move the monthly snapshots to EBS Snapshots Archive: full snapshots kept at much lower storage cost for long retention, restore takes up to 72 hours, minimum 90-day retention fits seven years.

Daily snapshots copied to a second Region (cross-Region snapshot copy, e.g. via Data Lifecycle Manager); after a Regional failure, create a volume from the copy and launch an instance there. No running standby needed for an RTO of hours.
